front: Can a server also be an endpoint?
back: Yes. An endpoint originates or receives traffic; a server is an endpoint supplying a service such as HTTP to clients.

front: What addresses guide Layer 2 switching and IP routing?
back: Layer 2 switching uses destination MAC addresses within a VLAN. Routing uses the destination IP address and a routing table.

front: What makes a switch a Layer 3 switch?
back: It supports IP routing as well as Ethernet switching. Routing must be configured; a management IP alone does not establish a forwarding role.

front: Which functions can one SOHO wireless router combine?
back: Ethernet switching, wireless access, IP routing and security functions. Diagnose the failed function rather than treating the whole enclosure as one role.

front: How do Catalyst Center and a wireless LAN controller differ?
back: Catalyst Center manages and monitors supported campus devices. A WLC coordinates supported APs and their wireless operation.

front: What does a next-generation firewall add to stateful filtering?
back: Capabilities such as application-aware policy and intrusion prevention. Inspectable traffic and enforcement depend on configuration and visibility.

front: How do IDS and inline IPS differ?
back: IDS detects and reports suspicious activity. An inline IPS can block traffic as it passes, according to policy; detection is not a guarantee against every attack.

front: In standards-based PoE, what are PSE and PD?
back: PSE supplies power; PD receives it. Detection checks for a compatible powered device before supplying normal operating power.

front: What two power limits must a PoE design satisfy?
back: The port must support the required allocation, and all allocations must fit the switch’s available total power budget.

front: Campus access, distribution and core: primary roles?
back: Access attaches endpoints; distribution aggregates access and often supplies routing/policy boundaries; core interconnects distribution blocks.
Two-tier combines distribution and core functions. Three-tier separates access, distribution and core; device count alone does not define the tiers.

front: Why do two physical uplinks not automatically guarantee redundancy?
back: They may share a failed device or other dependency. Trace both complete paths and verify that the design can use the surviving path.

front: What connects to what in a basic spine-leaf design?
back: Endpoints normally attach to leaves. Each leaf connects to every spine. This is the basic reference pattern, not a universal rule for every fabric variant.

front: What distinguishes a WAN from a local LAN?
back: A WAN connects networks across a wider geographic area, often through provider services. Local switching can remain operational when the WAN path fails.

front: How do on-premises hosting and cloud services differ?
back: On-premises names a location. Cloud names a service model with on-demand resources and elasticity; a private cloud can be on premises.
